final_candidates.decision_summary: Disrupts the PLP-binding lysine, a critical catalytic residue. AlphaMissense strongly predicts pathogenicity and MSA tolerance supports loss-of-function impact.
Cysteine 52 coordinates the heme cofactor; substituting it should destabilize the heme-binding pocket and abolish CBS activity. High phenotype score and low MSA frequency support a damaging effect.
Histidine 65 is a heme-ligand residue; mutation disrupts heme geometry and enzyme function. It shows the best PLM plausibility among top candidates and a strong AlphaMissense LOF signal.

stop_reason.detail: Additional evidence from functional annotations or other tools is unlikely to change the top three ranking, which is already well supported by phenotype and evolutionary data.

history.rationale: K119 is the PLP-binding lysine that forms the internal aldimine; replacing it with alanine removes the covalent cofactor attachment and should abolish catalytic activity.

Phenotype score is highest (0.987, pathogenic) and the mutation is at a strictly conserved PLP-binding lysine; low mutational frequency in MSA and low PLM plausibility further support loss-of-function.
Retains the strongest LOF phenotype signal and disrupts the PLP-binding lysine, directly aligning with the objective.
G307S is a well-characterized CBS pathogenic variant near the active-site/PLP environment and is associated with severe loss of enzyme activity.

Phenotype (0.828) and conservation (low MSA frequency) support a pathogenic effect; the position is a known CBS active-site residue, so it remains a strong candidate though slightly lower than the heme-ligand mutations.
Known CBS disease hotspot with high phenotype score, supporting loss-of-function for the requested top-three.
I278T is a common CBS missense mutation that severely impairs folding/stability and catalytic function in homocystinuria patients.

Despite low AlphaMissense prediction, this is a classic CBS LOF variant; very low MSA mutant frequency and high sequence-model surprise (low PLM) indicate evolutionary intolerance, so I retain it with adjusted confidence.
Despite being a known clinical CBS variant, the provided phenotype evidence is weak and lowers confidence; retain only as a backup due to established disease literature.
T191M is a known severe CBS mutation in the catalytic core; the bulky methionine likely disrupts local packing and diminishes/abolishes activity.
Moderate phenotype (0.716) and low PLM support a damaging effect; known disease-associated variant, though slightly lower priority than the top three.
Phenotype evidence is substantially stronger than the current lower-ranked I278T, so it should be moved up.
C52 is an axial heme ligand in the N-terminal domain; removing this coordination should destabilize the cofactor environment and impair CBS activity.
High phenotype (0.951) and low PLM plausibility support a damaging effect; C52 is a heme ligand, so mutation should abolish CBS activity despite moderate MSA mutant frequency.
High phenotype score and known heme-coordinating cysteine; substitution should strongly destabilize CBS activity.
H65 is the other reported heme coordination residue; loss of this ligand should perturb heme binding and reduce enzymatic competence.
Phenotype is high (0.845) and PLM plausibility is relatively lower; H65 is a heme ligand essential for stability and activity, supporting a loss-of-function substitution.
Strong phenotype support plus the best sequence_plm score among top candidates; potentially retained heme-ligand disruption.
A114 is immediately adjacent to the active-site loop containing K119; a valine substitution is expected to distort this region and impair PLP-dependent catalysis.
AlphaMissense predicts benign (0.287) and MSA frequency is moderate; low PLM alone is insufficient to outweigh the lack of phenotype support, so it is removed from active consideration.

rejection.reason: AlphaMissense predicts benign (0.287) and MSA frequency is moderate; low PLM alone is insufficient to outweigh the lack of phenotype support, so it is removed from active consideration.

history.rationale: P49L has been reported in the N-terminal heme domain and may disrupt CBS folding/cofactor stability, though the direct effect on activity is less strong.
AlphaMissense classifies it benign (0.087) and no other evidence suggests functional impact; low PLM is not sufficient, so it is rejected.
